findings.title: One h2 is a different size from the other 6
findings.evidence: “Famously straightforward and easy‑to‑use, there’s ” is 31px; the other h2s are 42px (31px ×1, 42px ×6). Same semantic level should get the same treatment.
findings.fix: Pick one size for h2 and set it once in CSS. If one of these is really a sub-heading, change its tag instead of its size.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: 565 words under 12px on a phone
findings.evidence: 71 text blocks render below 12px at 390px, e.g. a.skip-link “Skip to main content” at 11px.
findings.fix: Body text 16px on mobile; nothing readable under 12px. If the desktop size is in px, use clamp() or a mobile breakpoint.

findings.title: Social proof with no source (1)
findings.evidence: “99.99% uptime”. Round numbers of users, 4.9/5 ratings and 99.9% uptime on a new product are the template's defaults.
findings.fix: Use a number you can link to, or none. One true sentence beats three impressive ones.

findings.title: Fake macOS window dots
findings.evidence: Three red/yellow/green circles drawn in CSS to make a box look like a terminal or app window. Generated UIs use it to frame fake screenshots.
findings.fix: Show a real screenshot of the real thing, or a plain code block.

findings.title: 1 marketing buzzword
findings.evidence: “…’ve maintained an industry-leading record for years.…”
findings.fix: Replace each with the specific thing: what it does, for whom, with a number if you have one. 'Streamline your workflow' → 'Turns a 40-minute export into a button.'

hits: ’ve maintained an industry-leading record for years.

findings.title: 16 em dashes in 11.5k characters
findings.evidence: 1.4 per 1,000 characters. Humans use them; generated copy uses them in nearly every paragraph, and readers have learned to notice.
findings.fix: Keep the ones that do work; turn the rest into commas, periods, or parentheses.
findings.citation: Impeccable em-dash-overuse; Slopdar em-dash signal; HN thread

findings.title: 7 status dots on the page
findings.evidence: Coloured dots attached to labels where a word would say more.

findings.title: “How it works” in 4 numbered steps
findings.evidence: 4 siblings each lead with a number in a badge. The three-step setup strip was on 9% of Show HN launches; on a landing page it usually says less than one screenshot would.
findings.fix: Replace with the actual product: a screenshot, a 10-second clip, or the real command to run.
